findings.description: The user_data script contains a plaintext AWS access key and secret key. These are readable by anyone with EC2 describe-instance-attribute permissions and are committed to source control, so they must be treated as compromised.
No metadata_options block is defined to require IMDSv2 (http_tokens = required), leaving the legacy instance metadata service enabled and vulnerable to SSRF-based credential theft.
The EBS volume does not set encrypted = true (it is explicitly commented out), so data stored on the volume is unencrypted at rest.
The snapshot is created from the unencrypted web_host_storage volume, so the resulting snapshot is also unencrypted, exposing volume data at rest and to unauthorized copying.
Ingress rule allows TCP port 22 (SSH) from 0.0.0.0/0, exposing administrative access to the entire internet rather than restricting it to trusted source ranges.
Ingress rule allows TCP port 80 from 0.0.0.0/0 with no compensating controls (e.g., WAF, TLS), broadening the attack surface for the web application layer.
Egress rule permits all traffic (protocol -1, all ports) to 0.0.0.0/0, providing an unrestricted data exfiltration and command-and-control channel from the instance.
map_public_ip_on_launch = true automatically assigns public IP addresses to instances launched in this subnet, increasing exposure of workloads that may not need direct internet reachability.
map_public_ip_on_launch = true automatically assigns public IP addresses to instances launched in this subnet, increasing exposure of workloads that may not need direct internet reachability.
The S3 bucket storing VPC flow logs has no server_side_encryption_configuration, so log data (which can reveal network topology and traffic patterns) is stored unencrypted by default.
No aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block or bucket policy restricting access is defined for the flow log bucket, leaving it reliant on defaults and open to misconfiguration toward public exposure.
